push_stall.description: Whether a notifications `stall` event (an agent stalls) raises a notice on the founder's devices. The event is on the topic and in events.feed either way; the shell that raises notices reads this. null removes the key (back to the default).

push_account_out.description: Whether a notifications `account_out` event (an account is out) raises a notice on the founder's devices. The event is on the topic and in events.feed either way; the shell that raises notices reads this. null removes the key (back to the default).

host_active_cap.description: Most agents mid-turn at once on this machine, over every account; 0 is no limit. Over it the daemon starts no new work (status reason load). null removes the key (back to the default).

load_per_core_pct.description: Most 1-minute load per core, in percent (150 is 1.5 per core); 0 is off. Over it the daemon starts no new work. null removes the key (back to the default).

ram_free_min_pct.description: Least free memory, in percent of all; 0 is off. Under it the daemon starts no new work. null removes the key (back to the default).

host_simulator_hold.description: 1 holds the daemon's new work while a phone simulator or emulator runs on this machine; 0 does not. null removes the key (back to the default).

pacing.description: Hold each account to its weekly pace line (Account.pace): an account ahead of the line starts fewer turns, and one ahead by more than pace_burst_pct starts none (status reason pace) until the line catches up or another account has room. A turn a person starts is never held, and a running turn is never stopped. Off: only the windows' walls hold work. null removes the key (back to the default).

pace_target_pct.description: Where each account's pace line ends: its weekly usage, in percent, at the end of its week (its weekly reset, or its subscription end when that comes first). Under 100 because a reading lags by minutes. null removes the key (back to the default).

pace_burst_pct.description: How far, in points of the week, an account may run ahead of its pace line. Inside it the account's cap shrinks in step; past it the account starts no new turn. null removes the key (back to the default).

heavy_slots.description: How many heavy runs (test and build slots, tools/heavy-slot.sh) may hold a slot at once on this machine. The count is read from the config.yaml of the home the process runs in, and the slots are one lock per machine: two homes on one machine share it, so set the same number in both. HANDLINE_HEAVY_SLOTS in the environment overrides it. A change reaches the next run without a restart. null removes the key (back to the default).

keep_awake.description: Keep the machine from idle sleep: off; on (held while the daemon runs); working (held while an agent is mid-turn, released when the last one stops). The daemon holds macOS caffeinate -i; closing the lid still sleeps. Applied at the next tick, without a restart. null removes the key (back to the default).

reap_orphans.description: What the daemon does with work its agents left running after its parent died (headless Chrome, vitest, vite, a go test binary, yes, Electron) that has run 30 minutes under a worktree: dry (the default) only logs and records an orphan_would_stop event every 10 minutes; on stops it and records orphan_stopped; off does nothing. Nothing outside a worktree is touched.

SettingsChanges.description: settings.set's changes: any of SettingsValues' keys; null removes one.

MethodInfo.description: One method as a daemon lists it: its role and whether this caller may call it.

CellColor.description: An xterm palette index (0-15 are the client's theme ANSI colours, 16-255 the fixed cube and greys) or a true colour as lower-case `#rrggbb`. A colour the cell does not have (the default) is left out, never sent as a number.

SpanStyle.description: Only what differs from the default cell: a flag is sent as true or left out, a colour is left out for the default. `inverse` is sent as the flag, not applied: the client swaps the foreground and background it draws, so default colours swap too. A client ignores a key it does not know.

AttachmentId.description: Chosen by the daemon when an upload completes.

DebugTerminalPane.description: One pane of the terminal host, with what the daemon knows of it. A field the daemon does not know is null.

window.description: The window's index in its session.

terminal.description: The pane's handle, as terminal.attach takes it.

command.description: What the host says runs in the pane now.

idle_s.description: Seconds since the pane's window last drew output.

process.description: agent: an agent CLI (claude, codex, opencode) runs at or under the pane's process; shell: none does and the pane shows a shell; unknown: the process table could not be read and the pane's command says neither.

agent.description: The agent whose current terminal this pane is.

orphan.description: No agent has this pane as its terminal.

closed.description: The agent is closed; it keeps the handle of the pane it had.

recorded_agent.description: For an orphan: the agent the daemon opened the pane for.

cache_until.description: When the agent's prompt cache lapses, from its view.

orca_terminal.description: Always null: the daemon keeps no link from a tmux pane to an Orca terminal.

TextPart.description: Words of a task's text between its image references.

ImagePart.description: An image a task's text names, where it names it.

image.description: The Attachment; only `id` when the image is gone.

caption.description: The words in the reference's brackets; what a client shows when it cannot draw the image.

gone.description: true when the image is no longer kept: the client shows the caption without a picture.

path.description: Where the image is stored. Only for an agent caller, which reads it by path; a member or founder client never gets it.

removed.description: true when the founder deleted the image (attachment.remove), always with gone: the client says it was deleted.

RequestRef.description: The request's ref: 12 lowercase hex characters, unique and not guessable from another request's. The integer id stays the request's key everywhere else.

served_by.description: Which process answered. A daemon behind a gateway has no listener of its own; ask the gateway's local socket for the gateway's.

address.description: The host:port a pairing names (-advertise, else where the listener binds).

encryption.description: none is Tailscale mode: plain ws on a Tailscale or loopback address.

fingerprint.description: sha256 of the certificate presented; null in Tailscale mode.

tailscale_host.description: The address's host when it is a *.ts.net name, else null.

listener.description: The network listener of this process; null when it has none.

slots.description: HANDLINE_HEAVY_SLOTS as this process sees it, default 2.

dir.description: Where the slot locks are kept: HANDLINE_HEAVY_DIR, else ~/.handline/heavy-slots.

ConnectionInfo.description: How this process is reached, read only.

RequestName.description: A request named by its integer id, or by its ref: msg_ and the 12 hex characters, or the hash alone, or a prefix of at least 6 of them that begins only one request the caller may read (an ambiguous one is bad_request). A request the caller may not read is not_found, the same answer as one that does not exist.

Resources.description: What the machine and each agent use, measured every 15 s: one ps read for every agent. A figure the daemon could not read is 0.

cpu_pct.description: CPU in percent of one core, summed over the tree (ps %cpu): over 100 on several cores.

rss_bytes.description: Resident memory summed over the tree.

agents.description: Per agent with a terminal pane: its pane process and every process under it.

ram_free_bytes.description: Free for use: macOS free, inactive and speculative pages; Linux MemAvailable.

load_1m.description: The 1-minute load average; compare with cores.

disk_free_bytes.description: Free space of the volume the daemon home is on.

load_per_core.description: load_1m divided by cores; the load limit is compared with this (150 percent is 1.5).

ram_free_pct.description: ram_free_bytes in percent of ram_total_bytes; the free-memory floor is compared with this.

cpu_pct.description: CPU in percent of one core, summed over every agent's tree.

rss_bytes.description: Resident memory summed over every agent's tree.

agents_total.description: What all agents with a terminal pane use together.

start_hold.description: Why the daemon starts no new work now (the machine is over a load limit: text names the limit, as the status reason load does), null when starts may go. Level-triggered on the same measure; a machine with no agent mid-turn never holds.

NavPrefs.description: How the person's agent list and dock show agents, the same on every device.

pins.description: Pinned agents in the person's order: the dock shows them first and the list on top. No name twice.

unread_only.description: The list shows only agents with something unread or waiting on the person.

hidden.description: State groups the list hides: needs (waiting, blocked), working, waking, idle, sleeping (parked, none).

layout.description: tree: team, lead, members by parent. flat: urgency first, then by name.

order.description: The person's order for the tree layout: agents under one parent, and the top-level agents, stand in this order; one not listed (a new agent) comes after the listed ones, by name. The flat layout ignores it. No name twice.

NavPrefsChanges.description: Any keys of NavPrefs; each given key replaces the stored value whole.

pins.description: Pinned agents in the person's order: the dock shows them first and the list on top. No name twice.

unread_only.description: The list shows only agents with something unread or waiting on the person.

hidden.description: State groups the list hides: needs (waiting, blocked), working, waking, idle, sleeping (parked, none).

layout.description: tree: team, lead, members by parent. flat: urgency first, then by name.

order.description: The person's order for the tree layout: agents under one parent, and the top-level agents, stand in this order; one not listed (a new agent) comes after the listed ones, by name. The flat layout ignores it. No name twice.

Prefs.description: The person's view preferences, one set for the founder's devices, kept by the daemon. A new daemon serves the defaults: no pins, unread_only false, hidden empty, layout tree, collapsed empty, order empty.

cursor.description: The newest stream cursor when this read began. An event above it may be in the answer already (applying it again changes nothing); none at or below it is missing. A client drops the events at or below it for this answer.

MachineNeed.description: Something the machine needs of the founder, which no agent has: not a task and not an inbox message.

kind.description: disk: free space is under the floor (config disk_free_min_gb, default 5), so builds and tests wait. It stays until space is back over the floor plus 2 GB.

text.description: The item in plain words, with the free space in it.

orphan_worktrees.description: disk only, when there are any: the worktrees no agent works in (worktrees.list orphan), as housekeeping last measured them (at most hourly). The text names them too.

AttachmentRemoved.description: attachment.remove deleted this image or file: a client marks every ImagePart and MemoFile with this id gone and removed, without refetching.

bad_request.data: {code, field?, method?}; also JSON-RPC parse errors (-32700), invalid params (-32602) and an unknown method (-32601, data.method).

daemon_down.data: {code, log_path}; raised by the client library, never sent on the wire.

methods.name: hello
methods.summary: First call on every connection: versions and who the caller is.

schema.description: The protocol the client will speak.
The founder key, from the founder's own key file; local socket only. Wrong key: refused, gate `role`.
The git sha the client was built from. When it is not the daemon's own, the daemon logs it once on this connection; nothing is refused.

min_client.description: Oldest client protocol it still serves.

daemon.description: The loaded build's identity: its git sha, or <version>+<sha>[-dirty] for a release build.

version.description: The same build identity as `daemon`, under the name daemon.status uses, so a client compares its own build with one field.

exe.description: The absolute path of the executable this process runs.

methods.description: A client whose protocol is below min_client gets `refused` (gate `protocol`) with hint `hl service install`. A newer client gets a normal reply and decides itself whether to run. Any other call before hello is bad_request. Role by proof: a matching `key` gives founder; with no key, a peer pid that verifies against a recorded session gives agent; a device token (network listener) gives member; anything else is anonymous and every method but hello is refused until a later hello proves more. On the network listener a hello without a valid `token` is refused, gate `unpaired`, with no data; with one it is member.

methods.name: whoami
methods.summary: The viewer, the device, the role and the methods allowed.

methods.description: The same list hello gives, with allowed flags for this caller.

methods.name: subscribe
methods.summary: Turn the connection into a stream of `event` notices; replays after `since` first, unless `resume` is latest.

schema.description: Last cursor seen. Absent: live only. A cursor older than the daemon keeps, or with more than 5000 subscribed events after it, is answered by a `gap` notice (reason retention) instead of a replay; the connection stays open. Up to 5000 events behind, every missed event is replayed in full, in cursor order, before any live one.

replay (the default): what was missed after `since` is sent first, as `since` says. latest: nothing missed is sent, neither a replay nor a gap; the reply's cursor is the newest and only later events follow. A client that resumes at the latest reads again what it shows: each read a stream event keeps current says its `cursor`, and an event at or below it is in that answer already.
Only events of this agent, plus events that carry no agent. Meant for the chat topic.

cursor.description: The newest cursor at subscribe time.

methods.description: topics is a non-empty list of known topics, else -32602 bad_request naming `topics`. Notices start only after this reply is sent. devices is subscribed on its own, by the founder: a topics list naming devices and any other topic is -32602 bad_request naming `topics`, because devices is served by the gateway itself and every other topic by the daemon behind it. A devices subscription is live only: `since` and `agent` are ignored, the reply cursor is 0, its events carry cursor 0, and a client that reconnects reads devices.list again. The transcript topic needs member, as transcript.events does: an agent session that names it is refused, gate role, and nothing is subscribed (the stream holds every agent's tool inputs and results).

methods.name: unsubscribe
methods.summary: Stop some topics; a subscription with no topics left ends. Result {}.
methods.description: Naming devices follows the same rule as subscribe: on its own.

methods.name: daemon.status
methods.summary: Status bar: alive, versions, terminal host, agent counts, inbox count.

methods.name: events.feed
methods.summary: Resumable feed of events with their deep-link targets; the polling twin of subscribe.

gap.description: True when `since` is older than retention; refetch snapshots.

methods.description: topics defaults to [notifications]; limit defaults to 50, at most 200. Without `since`: the newest events, oldest first. With `since`: the events after it; if `since` is older than retention the feed starts at the oldest kept event and `gap` is true. cursor is the newest cursor in the reply, or the current newest when there are no events.

methods.name: debug.terminals
methods.summary: Every pane of the terminal host with what the daemon knows of it, for the hidden debug window.
methods.description: Lists every pane of the daemon's terminal server (tmux), whichever agent has it or none, to find panes kept open past their prompt cache and shells left behind after an agent's session exited. Reads only: the host's pane list, the process table and the daemon's own rows; of the agent's view only cache_until. A host that cannot list its panes is refused, gate unsupported; one that cannot be reached, gate state. Watching a listed pane is terminal.attach by its handle; a pane no agent has takes no input. Callers: the founder and a paired device (member); below that is refused, gate role.

methods.name: prefs.get
methods.summary: The person's view preferences: the agent list's pins, filter, layout and folds.

methods.name: prefs.set
methods.summary: Change the person's view preferences: each key given in changes.nav replaces the stored one.
methods.description: A pin, a fold or an order entry naming an agent the daemon does not know, or a name given twice, is bad_request naming the field. Once stored, a prefs.changed event on the prefs topic carries the whole Prefs. agent.retire drops the agent from pins, collapsed and order (and sends prefs.changed); a rename (hr) carries it over in place.

methods.name: hook.record
methods.summary: A hook records an event; the spool replays it with the same request_id.

methods.name: memory.status
methods.summary: Per-agent memory against its budget (hl memory status).

methods.name: connection.get
methods.summary: How this process is reached: its listener, the heavy-run slots and dev mode. Read only.

methods.name: daemon.upgrade
methods.summary: Restart the daemon onto a given handlined: the app's half of one update replacing app and daemon together.

schema.description: Absolute path of the handlined to run.
The git sha that binary was built from.

methods.description: The daemon runs `exe --version` (30 s at most) and refuses, gate `build`, unless the binary starts and prints `sha` (a checkout build prints the sha, a release <version>+<sha>[-dirty]); it then keeps running as it was. A binary that passes: the reply is sent, the tick in hand finishes, the lock and the database are given up as a clean stop gives them up, and the process execs `exe` with its own arguments. The client then sees the connection end and reconnects; the new daemon's hello and daemon.status carry the new version. A retry with the same request_id gets the kept reply and does not restart again. Served on the local socket only: a paired device does not choose the binary the machine runs.

methods.name: settings.get
methods.summary: Timings, terminal host, trust folders, hooks installed.

schema.description: Return that agent's own overrides in `overrides`.

methods.name: settings.set
methods.summary: Change settings: any keys of SettingsValues, globally or as one agent's override.

schema.description: Write the per-agent override of: park_timeout_s, ignore_cache_expiry, bg_notice_s, bg_grace_s, bg_check_s, notice_digest_s, handoff_prompt. Any other key with `agent` is bad_request.
